description: The chart illustrates how perplexity varies across different sparsity rates for two methods shown as paired bars. The horizontal axis contains the categories labeled “Sparsity Rate,” ordered from 10% through 80% in 10% increments. The vertical axis is labeled “Perplexity” and uses a logarithmic scale with major tick marks at approximately \(10^1\), \(10^2\), and \(10^3\), spanning from just below 10 up to about 1000. For each sparsity rate, two adjacent bars are shown: a blue bar labeled “Per-Output” in the legend and an orange bar (legend entry appears blank/unlabeled). At 10% sparsity, both bars are near about 5–6 perplexity; at 20% and 30% they remain around roughly 5–6; at 40% they are around ~6–7; at 50% around ~7–8; at 60% around ~9–11; at 70% the blue bar is around ~20 while the orange bar is around ~35–40; and at 80% the blue bar is around ~500–600 while the orange bar is around ~900–1000. The bars are grouped side-by-side for each sparsity category (not stacked), there are no visible error bars or annotations, and no bars appear specially emphasized beyond the consistent color coding.
